verdict.rationale: The evidence clearly documents starting Copilot cloud agent tasks from GitHub: you can assign tasks, mention @copilot on pull requests, launch work from GitHub, and trigger runs from repository events. The other named surfaces are thin. 'Project tools, chat apps' is a generic claim that never names Linear or Slack, and GitLab is not mentioned at all. Missing for 10: documented Slack trigger, documented Linear trigger, any GitLab support, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can kick off agent tasks directly from GitHub, GitLab, Linear, or Slack

citations.quote: Mention `@copilot` in a comment on an existing pull request to ask it to make changes.
Launch work from GitHub, track progress across multiple agents, review changes, and merge completed work
Assign tasks to agents like Copilot, Claude by Anthropic, and OpenAI Codex, and let them plan, explore, and execute work autonomously in the background.
Set up an automation to run Copilot automatically, on a schedule or in response to events such as an issue being opened.
Copilot works where you do—in GitHub, your IDE, the CLI, project tools, chat apps, and custom MCP servers.
